summary: This bill suspends federal excise taxes on gasoline, diesel fuel, and kerosene for 120 days after enactment (extendable by 90 days at the President's discretion), transfers equivalent revenue from the general fund to the Highway Trust Fund and Leaking Underground Storage Tank Trust Fund, and authorizes enforcement to ensure the savings reach consumers.

scores.thoughts: The bill suspends fuel excise taxes but requires the Treasury to transfer equivalent amounts from the general fund to the Highway Trust Fund and Leaking Underground Storage Tank Trust Fund. This maintains existing trust-fund spending levels without any net expansion or reduction in overall federal outlays. The legislation does not address appropriations, program funding, or spending cuts/increases, so it has no meaningful bearing on government spending.

Section 2(a) explicitly sets the federal excise tax rates on gasoline, diesel, and kerosene to zero for 120 days (extendable by 90 days) and suspends the Leaking Underground Storage Tank financing rate. This is a direct, across-the-board reduction in fuel taxes, with enforcement provisions to ensure the savings reach consumers. The bill therefore strongly advances lower taxes.
The bill contains no provisions related to health insurance, medical providers, public health programs, or healthcare financing.
The bill contains no provisions related to firearms, background checks, or gun regulations.
The bill contains no provisions related to visas, border security, asylum, or immigration enforcement.
The bill contains no provisions related to reproductive health services or abortion access.
The bill contains no provisions related to defense appropriations or military spending.
The bill contains no provisions that alter environmental regulations, emissions standards, or conservation programs. Any indirect effect on fuel consumption is outside the text of the legislation.
The bill contains no provisions related to welfare programs, SNAP, housing assistance, or other safety-net benefits.
The bill contains no provisions related to schools, student aid, or education funding.
The bill contains no provisions related to controlled substances or drug enforcement.
The bill contains no provisions related to sentencing, policing, or criminal justice reform.
The bill contains no provisions related to tariffs, trade agreements, or import/export policy.

By reducing dedicated fuel-tax revenue while requiring the general fund to backfill the affected trust funds, the bill increases the federal deficit for the duration of the tax holiday. However, the measure is narrowly targeted and temporary, so the effect on debt-reduction priorities is modest.
The bill contains no provisions related to LGBTQ+ legal protections or rights.
The bill contains no provisions related to foreign assistance or international aid.
The bill contains no provisions related to voting access, election administration, or campaign finance.
The bill contains no provisions related to technology regulation, data privacy, or cybersecurity.
The bill contains no provisions related to collective bargaining, worker protections, or union rules.
The bill contains no provisions related to religious exemptions or anti-discrimination law.
